title: Uttara Swami Malai Temple Delhi - History, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Uttara Swami Malai Temple - Delhi,

Uttara Swami Malai Temple, also known as Malai Mandir, is one of the most famous South Indian temples in Delhi, dedicated to Lord Murugan (Kartikeya). Located in RK Puram, the temple is built in traditional Dravidian style and stands beautifully on a small hill, giving it a grand presence.

The temple was established in the 1970s by the Tamil community of Delhi and has since become an important cultural and spiritual center. Its towering gopurams, intricate carvings, and peaceful surroundings make it feel like a piece of South India in the heart of Delhi. Along with Lord Murugan, the temple also has shrines of Lord Ganesha, Lord Shiva, Goddess Meenakshi, and other deities.

Special Highlight: The temple is most vibrant during Thaipusam and Skanda Shashti, when devotees gather in large numbers to celebrate with music, rituals, and devotion.

Best Time to Visit: You can visit the Uttara Swami Malai Temple any time of the year, but the best time is from October to March, when the weather is pleasant for exploring Delhi.

How to Reach Uttara Swami Malai Temple:

  • Nearest Metro Station: Dhaula Kuan (Airport Express Line) or Hauz Khas (Yellow Line), followed by a short auto/cab ride.
  • By Road: Easily accessible by car, taxi, or bus. Parking is available near the temple.
  • Nearby Attractions: Hauz Khas Village, Qutub Minar, and Garden of Five Senses.

Visitor Information:

  • Timings: Open daily from 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM.
  • Entry Fee: Free for all visitors.
  • Dress Code: Modest and traditional clothing is recommended.

Travel Tip: Remove footwear before entering and take a moment to admire the detailed carvings—they tell entire mythological stories in stone.

faqs.question: What makes Uttara Swami Malai Temple unique?
faqs.answer: It is one of the few temples in North India dedicated to Lord Murugan (Kartikeya) and is built in traditional South Indian Dravidian style.

faqs.question: Can tourists and non-Hindus visit the temple?
faqs.answer: Yes, the temple welcomes all visitors, regardless of religion, to admire its architecture and experience its peaceful atmosphere.

faqs.question: What are the timings of Uttara Swami Malai Temple?
faqs.answer: The temple is open daily from 6:00 AM – 12:00 PM and 5:00 PM – 9:00 PM.

faqs.question: Which festivals are celebrated at Uttara Swami Malai Temple?
faqs.answer: Major festivals include Thaipusam and Skanda Shashti, when the temple is beautifully decorated and full of devotees.

faqs.question: How can I reach Malai Mandir in Delhi?
faqs.answer: The nearest metro station is Vasant Vihar (Magenta Line), and from there, visitors can take an auto or cab to the temple.
